title: release-gate-probe negative control is stale (0.14.1 accepts [targets]) and its Windows extract fails on a D:\ tar path
description: Measured on release.yml publish=false dispatches 39826035054 (#646 head a021f560) and 39831687843 (dev 2769973e, the control): both reproduce the same two reds in all six release gate probe jobs, so neither comes from LCLI-750. (1) linux/darwin: the previous release (npm latest 0.14.1) now accepts [targets], so `--expect absent` exits 0 where the probe requires `Unrecognized key: "targets"`; the negative control must be re-based on a release that actually rejects the feature, or on another feature. (2) win32: GNU tar in Git bash reads `D:\a\_temp\...` as host:path ("tar: D\:\a\\_temp/lore-release-gate-probe-fresh-win32-x64: Cannot open", exit 2), so the Windows legs never reach the probe; the extract must use a path tar accepts (relative, or --force-local). Floor work: scripts/release-gate-probe.mjs and release.yml, needs a reviewer pass. setup-quest itself is fine on win32 (installed 0.14.1 from npm and asserted it).
implementationNotes: Scope narrowed pending an opum-doc ruling: this PR fixes only the win32 extract (tar -C with D:\ RUNNER_TEMP read as host:path); the stale-control half cannot be built because git diff v0.14.1..HEAD -- src .lore is empty, so no feature exists that the fresh binary accepts and 0.14.1 rejects. Reported to team-lead.

opum-doc RULED A (relayed by team-lead, 2026-10-22 ~18:55Z): keep the gate as designed; with zero binary delta (v0.14.1..origin/dev over src, .lore, bin/ and package.json empty, against a positive control of 45 files across all paths) a red gate is the correct answer, and no stand-in feature is invented. PRECONDITION OF THE NEXT RELEASE CUT: the first release carrying new binary behaviour re-bases the negative control onto that feature, and must show the previous release (npm latest) rejecting it with the exact expected message, as a RED line in the publish=false dispatch log; do not rediscover this as a red dispatch. This PR delivers only the win32 extract half (proof: dispatch 39835331510 on the branch, win32-x64 and win32-arm64 legs passed the extract and ran the fresh arm: "lore.exe check ... exited 0, as required (targets is present)", then went red at the stale control as expected). The stale-control half stays open on this record.

Win32 extract half LANDED: opum-ai/lore-cli#648, squash c35ec7e0da2f7ab623d7755f7191175519fd5835 on origin/dev (Opus review APPROVE at b6d4b021; proof dispatch 39835331510). The stale-control half stays OPEN per opum-doc ruling A (see the precondition note above): the first release carrying new binary behaviour re-bases the negative control.

Parked 2026-10-23: win32 extract half landed (#648). The stale-control half cannot be built until a release carries new binary behaviour (v0.14.1..origin/dev over src, .lore, bin/, package.json is empty). Per opum-doc ruling A the gate stays red by design; the first release with new binary behaviour must re-base the negative control onto that feature, showing npm latest rejecting it with the exact message in a publish=false dispatch. Not waiting on a plan; waiting on that release. Release held.
